evidence.note: R9efb011c9b CONFIRMED: fold gave two 'lost prompt'; export sessions showed it twice

commit 69f9bcd: fold skips session.prompt/note events named by another event's adopted_from

chunk_findings.detail: The dedupe keys on the *id value* rather than on the specific orphan event. Since orphans are id-less, every orphan's `id` is the empty string `""`, so once any orphan is adopted the set becomes `adopted == {""}` (the copy's `adopted_from` points at the original's id, which is `""`). From then on the guard drops *every* session.prompt/session.note whose id is `""` — including orphans that were never adopted. Concrete scenario: run `log.append("session.prompt", "", {"text": "lost prompt", "item": ""})`, adopt it via `session adopt-orphans` (recorded `adopted_from == ""`), then later append a *second*, unadopted orphan `log.append("session.prompt", "", {"text": "new orphan", "item": ""})`; `fold(log.read_all())` silently discards `"new orphan"` (`"" in adopted` is true), so the text vanishes from all fold readers including export sessions. The new test `test_an_unadopted_orphan_is_still_folded` passes only because it never creates an adoption in the same log, giving false confidence. Skipping needs to match event identity (or at least only skip the orphan that is actually referenced), not the shared `""` id.

chunk_findings.detail:
The dedup key is a value that is not unique per orphan, so once *one* orphan has been adopted, every other id-less `session.prompt`/`session.note` is silently dropped from folded state, not just the adopted original.

Concretely: the code skips any session-text event whose `ev.id` is in `adopted`, where `adopted` is the set of `adopted_from` values harvested from the copies. For this skip to fire on the id-less original at all (as the new tests require — `out.count("lost prompt") == 1` only passes if the original is skipped), the original's `ev.id` must equal the `adopted_from` value written by `session adopt-orphans`. But the original is id-less (that is the whole premise in the comment and the intent), so that key is a shared constant (`""`/`None`) — or, if ids are content-derived, a key shared by every event with identical text. Either way it is not unique to one orphan.

Demonstration: with the repo from `_adopted_repo`, run `session adopt-orphans` (copy now carries `adopted_from`), then append a *second*, never-adopted orphan, e.g. `log.append("session.prompt", "", {"text": "later orphan", "item": ""})`, and call `fold(log.read_all(), strict=False)`. Because the second orphan's `ev.id` is the same id-less value that is now in `adopted`, it hits `continue` and never reaches the handler: `st.sessions[""].prompts` no longer contains `"later orphan"`, and `export sessions` silently omits it. Same result for a pre-existing unadopted orphan that survives alongside an adopted one — exactly the mixed case the new test file avoids, since `test_an_unadopted_orphan_is_still_folded` only exercises a log with *no* adopted event at all (empty `adopted` set), which is the one configuration where the defect cannot appear.

The fix has to key on something that actually identifies the specific source event (or gate the skip on the orphan being the one referenced), rather than membership of a value shared by all id-less text events.
